Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns completeness of the Subchapter L filing/election archive; escalation to Tax Director

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IRC §6001 recordkeeping requirement plus the specific Subchapter L election sections relied on in the year's return (§807, §831(b), §846), re-read at archiving time

In-scope processes.value: Annual Form 1120-L filing close-out → retention archiving, covering every return, election statement and IRS approval/acceptance correspondence for the filing year

In-scope systems.value: Primary archive for as-filed returns and elections; the compliance evidence repository holds the retention index and legal holds

Compliance procedure documented.value: Tax Record Retention Procedure — inventory, retrieval, reconciliation to the GL, retention labeling, access control and annual purge review

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and Compliance Officer; reviewed annually and on any change to the IRS statute-of-limitations exposure

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Archiving must close within 30 days of the return's e-file acceptance; retention date computed as filing date + 7 years, or exam-close date if later

Deadline reminders configured.value: Retention schedule report flags folders approaching their retention date 90 days ahead of the annual purge review

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: As-filed returns, election statements, e-file acknowledgments and IRS exam correspondence retained 7 years from filing or until any exam/litigation closes, whichever is later

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing documents, access-control gaps and premature purges logged as exceptions with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Compliance Officer signs the annual retention completeness attestation and any remediation item for missing evidence

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every tax year within the current retention window with a filed Form 1120-L, plus every Subchapter L election logged in the election register for those years

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a missing as-filed return or election statement in a year under open exam; ≤2% missing-document rate tolerated elsewhere before escalation

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; test runs annually over the full retention population plus 100% of open-exam years

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed any retrieval or archiving step for the sampled years

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual retention test workpaper (population extract, sample, retrieval notes, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Retained-filing index plus IRS e-file acknowledgments, presentable to an IRS examiner within 10 business days of an Information Document Request

Regulator response path.value: Tax Director owns the IDR response; General Counsel clears any document release involving a closed exam position

checklist.step: Identify every return, election and approval artifact requiring retention for the filing cycle
actions: Pull the filed-return list from Tax Manager for the tax year (Form 1120-L, consolidated Form 1120 if part of a life/non-life group, Form 8926 for corporate-owned life insurance excise if applicable).
List every election made in that year's return: accounting method changes under §807/§846, reserve computation method, any §831(b) election for a captive subsidiary, consolidated-return election.
Note any IRS correspondence received in the year: exam notices, RAR, closing agreements, PLR responses.
Cross-check the list against the Tax Department's election log maintained in Microsoft Excel.
checklist.done: a complete inventory of returns, elections and IRS correspondence for the tax year exists with nothing omitted from the election log.

checklist.step: Retrieve the as-filed return package including all Subchapter L schedules
actions: Pull the final e-filed Form 1120-L, Schedule L balance sheet, Schedule F reserve computation and Schedule H (if applicable) from the return-preparation output.
Confirm the version matches what was transmitted by comparing the file timestamp to the e-file transmission log.
Attach the IRS e-file acceptance acknowledgment (Submission ID plus 'Accepted' status).
Save the set as <company>-1120L-<taxyear>-AS-FILED in the document management repository.
checklist.done: the as-filed return, its schedules and the matching e-file acceptance acknowledgment are archived under one filing folder.

checklist.step: Archive every accounting-method and reserve election statement attached to the return
actions: Open the return's election-statements section and copy out each §807/§846/§831(b) election statement verbatim.
Confirm each statement cites the correct Code section and states the effective tax year.
File each election statement as its own document, cross-referenced to the return it was filed with.
Log the election, its Code section and its effective year in the Tax Department's election register.
checklist.done: every election statement is filed individually and logged in the election register with its Code section and effective year.

checklist.step: Collect IRS approval and acceptance correspondence tied to the filing
actions: Gather the IRS e-file acceptance record for the electronically filed return.
Gather any IRS letter or notice confirming receipt of a ruling request, an accounting-method change (Form 3115 consent) or an extension (Form 7004 confirmation).
Request from Tax Director any private letter ruling correspondence relevant to a Subchapter L position taken.
Scan and OCR paper correspondence so it is text-searchable.
checklist.done: all IRS acceptance/approval correspondence for the filing year is collected, OCR'd and ready for filing.

checklist.step: Reconcile the retained package to the general ledger tax provision
actions: Open the current and deferred tax provision accounts for the tax year in the ERP general ledger.
Agree the return's Schedule M adjustments and the Schedule F reserve deduction to the tax provision workpaper.
Flag and resolve any variance with the Tax Manager before the package is archived as final.
Note the reconciliation reference on the archive folder.
checklist.done: the archived return package reconciles to the GL tax provision with no unresolved variance.

checklist.step: File the package with the correct retention label and index metadata
actions: Apply the company retention schedule code for federal tax records (minimum 7 years from filing date, or until the IRS statute of limitations plus any extension closes, whichever is later) in the compliance evidence repository.
Index the folder by tax year, entity/NAIC co-code, and Code section for every election it contains.
Set a legal-hold flag if any exam is open for that year.
Confirm the retention date calculated by the system matches the manual computation.
checklist.done: the folder carries the correct retention date, full index metadata and any applicable legal hold.

checklist.step: Cross-reference the Appointed Actuary's opinion supporting the reserve deduction
actions: Request from the Appointed Actuary the signed statutory reserve opinion and the tax-basis reserve reconciliation workpaper used to support the Schedule F deduction.
Confirm the opinion date pre-dates the return filing date.
Attach the opinion and reconciliation to the archive folder with a cross-reference note on the return's Schedule F line.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary's opinion and reserve reconciliation are attached and dated before the filing date.

checklist.step: Track and archive any open IRS examination correspondence separately
actions: For any tax year under active IRS exam, open a separate exam-correspondence sub-folder.
Log each Information Document Request (IDR) received and the response filed against it.
Attach any Revenue Agent Report (RAR) and Form 870-AD or closing agreement once issued.
Keep the exam sub-folder under legal hold until the exam formally closes.
checklist.done: every open exam year has a dedicated, legal-held sub-folder with all IDRs, responses and any RAR/closing agreement.

checklist.step: Verify prior-year archived versions have not been altered
actions: For the prior three tax years' folders, run the repository's version-history report.
Confirm no document was modified after its retention-lock date.
Investigate any flagged modification with the document owner.
Record the verification in the annual retention audit log.
checklist.done: prior-year archives show no post-lock modification, or every flagged change is investigated and explained.

checklist.step: Escalate any missing election statement or unfiled acknowledgment
actions: Where an expected election statement or e-file acknowledgment cannot be located, raise the gap to Tax Director within 5 business days.
Determine whether the position was actually filed by pulling the IRS account transcript through the IRS e-Services Transcript Delivery System.
If the position was filed but evidence is missing, request a duplicate from the return preparer.
If the position was never filed, open a remediation item with Tax Director sign-off.
checklist.done: every missing-evidence gap is either resolved with a located document or converted into a signed remediation item.

checklist.step: Publish the retained-filing index to Compliance Ops
actions: Export the current index of retained returns, elections and correspondence from the compliance evidence repository.
Send the export to the Compliance Officer with the retention dates and any open legal holds highlighted.
Confirm receipt and log the publish date.
checklist.done: Compliance Ops holds a current, dated index of every retained filing artifact and open legal hold.

checklist.step: Confirm access controls on the archive match the sensitivity of tax records
actions: Review the repository's access-control list for the tax archive folder.
Restrict write/delete access to Tax Manager and Records Manager only.
Give read-only access to Internal Audit and the Compliance Officer.
Remove access for any departed employee within 5 business days of departure.
checklist.done: write access is limited to Tax Manager and Records Manager, and no departed employee retains access.

checklist.step: Perform the annual purge review against the retention schedule
actions: Run the retention schedule report to identify folders past their retention date with no open legal hold.
Confirm with Tax Director that no active exam or litigation applies to each candidate folder.
Obtain written sign-off before any purge is executed.
Log the purge decision (retain vs destroy) and the sign-off in the retention audit log.
checklist.done: every folder past its retention date has a documented, signed purge or extended-retention decision.

checklist.step: Sign off the annual retention completeness attestation
actions: Review the published index against the year's filed returns and election register for completeness.
Sign the annual retention completeness attestation confirming every required artifact is archived and correctly labeled.
File the signed attestation in the compliance evidence repository alongside the year's index.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation confirming archive completeness is filed with the year's index.

checklist.step: Report retention exceptions to the Compliance Committee
actions: Summarize any unresolved missing-document or access-control exceptions from the year.
Present the summary and remediation status at the next Compliance Committee sitting.
Record the committee's disposition and any follow-up date.
checklist.done: unresolved retention exceptions are reported to the Compliance Committee with a recorded disposition.

testing.step: Build the population of tax years and elections subject to the retention obligation
actions: Extract from the compliance evidence repository the list of all tax years with a filed Form 1120-L within the retention window.
Cross-check the count against the Tax Department's filing calendar.
Add every election logged in the election register for those years.
Reconcile the extract to the general ledger's tax provision entries for completeness.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the filing calendar and election register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the election register and filing calendar
actions: Match each population year to a corresponding election-register entry and filing-calendar entry.
List any tax year present in one source but not the other as an exception.
Confirm the reconciliation total ties before sampling begins.
testing.done: every population entry reconciles to both the election register and filing calendar, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of tax years currently under open IRS exam.
Take a random sample (seeded, reproducible) of 10 additional years/elections from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and includes every open-exam year.

testing.step: Re-perform the retrieval of each sampled return and election statement
actions: Independently locate the as-filed return, election statement and e-file acknowledgment for each sampled item in the document management repository without asking Tax for the folder location.
Confirm the retrieved document matches the description in the index.
Note any item that cannot be located within 30 minutes as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled document is independently located and matches the index, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the retention date and legal-hold status on each sampled folder
actions: Recompute the retention date for each sampled folder from its filing date and the retention policy (7 years from filing, or exam-close date if later).
Compare to the date recorded by the repository.
Check that any year under open exam correctly shows a legal hold.
testing.done: recomputed retention dates match the repository, and every open-exam year shows an active legal hold.

testing.step: Trace each sampled election to its supporting Code section and effective year
actions: Read the election statement and confirm it cites the correct Subchapter L Code section (e.g., §807, §831(b), §846) and states the correct effective tax year.
Confirm the election was actually reflected in the corresponding line of the filed return.
Flag any election statement with no return effect as unsupported.
testing.done: every sampled election traces to the correct Code section and is reflected in the filed return.

testing.step: Test access controls on the archive against the current access list
actions: Pull the current access-control list for the tax archive folder from the document management repository.
Compare against the active employee roster and current Tax Manager/Records Manager assignments.
Flag any access held by a departed employee or anyone outside the approved list.
testing.done: no access exception exists outside the approved Tax Manager/Records Manager list.

testing.step: Recompute the annual purge decision for folders past their retention date
actions: Identify folders past their computed retention date.
Confirm each has a documented, signed purge/extend decision.
Recompute whether an open exam or litigation should have blocked a purge that was executed.
testing.done: every folder past its retention date has a correctly signed decision and no premature purge occurred.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception describing the tax year, what was missing or incorrect, and the retention/compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (misfiled, never retained, access-control gap, incorrect retention date) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open exceptions into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missing-document threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer who did not perform the retrieval sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the cycle's withholding computation and remittance; escalation to Tax Director

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IRC §3405 (annuity/pension withholding), §1441/§1442 (NRA withholding), §3406 (backup withholding) and current Publication 15-T rate tables, re-read each processing cycle for rate changes

In-scope processes.value: Annuity/life/retirement distribution processing → withholding computation → EFTPS remittance → Form 945/1042 reporting, across all payees including foreign policyholders

In-scope systems.value: Source of distribution payments; withholding is computed and posted through the ERP general ledger before EFTPS remittance

Compliance procedure documented.value: Distribution Withholding & Remittance Procedure — election capture, rate computation, NRA/backup withholding, GL posting, EFTPS deposit, reconciliation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Tax Director; reviewed annually against updated IRS Publication 15-T tables and treaty rate schedules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Deposits due per the semi-weekly or monthly EFTPS schedule set by the 12-month lookback; Form 945 due January 31, Form 1042 and 1042-S due March 15

Deadline reminders configured.value: Treasury deposit calendar alerts at T-2 business days for semi-weekly deposits and the 12th of the month for monthly deposits

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Withholding batches, manager approvals, GL postings and EFTPS confirmations retained 7 years from the remittance date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed deposits, misapplied NRA rates and unresolved TIN issues logged as exceptions with penalty exposure and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Tax Director signs off every missed-deposit remediation and any treaty-rate correction

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All annuity, life cash-value and qualified-plan distributions paid in the test period, with NRA and backup-withholding flags applied

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a late EFTPS deposit or a misapplied NRA/treaty rate; any fail escalates to Tax Director

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per remittance cycle; test runs quarterly over that quarter's population plus 100% of NRA/backup-withholding payments

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have computed or approved any sampled withholding batch

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly withholding test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Withholding batch, EFTPS confirmations and Form 945/1042 filings, presentable to an IRS examiner within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Tax Director owns the IRS deposit/withholding inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any penalty-abatement submission

checklist.step: Identify distributions and payments subject to Subchapter L withholding this cycle
actions: Run the distributions report in the policy administration system for the processing cycle, filtering to annuity periodic/nonperiodic payments, life insurance cash surrenders, and IRA/retirement distributions.
Flag any payment to a non-U.S. address or with a Form W-8BEN on file for NRA withholding review.
Flag any payee record missing a valid TIN for backup withholding review.
Export the flagged population to the Tax Analyst.
checklist.done: the cycle's distribution population is extracted with NRA and missing-TIN flags applied.

checklist.step: Confirm the payee's withholding election is current
actions: For periodic annuity payments, check the payee's Form W-4P election on file and its effective date.
For nonperiodic distributions, check the Form W-4R election.
Where no election is on file, apply the IRS default withholding rate for the payment type and log the applied default on the payment record.
Confirm the default calculation matches current IRS withholding guidance for the payment type.
checklist.done: every payment shows either a current election or the correctly applied IRS default, logged on the record.

checklist.step: Compute the federal withholding amount per payment
actions: Apply the elected or default withholding rate to the gross distribution amount per the current IRS Publication 15-T periodic/nonperiodic withholding tables.
For IRA/qualified-plan rollovers eligible for direct-rollover treatment, confirm zero withholding applies and the rollover paperwork is on file.
Record the computed withholding amount against the payment record.
checklist.done: every in-scope payment carries a computed withholding amount consistent with the election/default and rollover status.

checklist.step: Apply NRA withholding to foreign-payee payments
actions: For payments flagged as NRA, check for a valid Form W-8BEN claiming a treaty rate.
Where valid, apply the treaty withholding rate and record the treaty article.
Where absent or expired, apply the statutory 30% rate under IRC §1441.
Log the payee's country and treaty basis on the payment record.
checklist.done: every NRA payment applies either the verified treaty rate or the 30% statutory rate, with the basis logged.

checklist.step: Apply backup withholding where a TIN is missing or flagged
actions: For payments flagged missing/invalid TIN, apply 24% backup withholding under IRC §3406.
Send a B-Notice to the payee requesting a corrected Form W-9.
Log the B-Notice date and the 30-day cure due date on the payee record.
checklist.done: every missing/invalid-TIN payment has backup withholding applied and a dated B-Notice on file.

checklist.step: Route the computed withholding batch for manager review
actions: Pull the cycle's withholding computation batch and re-check a sample of the largest 10 payments for correct rate application.
Confirm the batch total withholding ties to the sum of individual payment withholding amounts.
Approve the batch for remittance or return exceptions to the Tax Analyst for correction.
checklist.done: the batch is reviewed, ties to individual amounts, and is approved or returned with corrections.

checklist.step: Post the withholding liability to the general ledger
actions: Post the withholding liability from the approved batch to the federal withholding payable account, split by domestic (§3405/§3406) and NRA (§1441) sub-accounts.
Reconcile the posted total to the batch approval.
Attach the batch approval as the posting support.
checklist.done: the withholding liability is posted to the correct GL sub-accounts and reconciles to the approved batch.

checklist.step: Remit the withheld tax to the IRS within the deposit deadline
actions: Determine the deposit schedule (semi-weekly or monthly) from the prior lookback period's total withholding liability.

Initiate the federal tax deposit through EFTPS before the applicable deadline (semi-weekly deposits due the Wednesday/Friday following the payment date; monthly deposits due the 15th of the following month).
Record the EFTPS confirmation number against the batch.
checklist.done: the deposit is submitted through EFTPS before its deadline with a confirmation number on file.

checklist.step: Reconcile the EFTPS deposit to the GL withholding liability
actions: Pull the EFTPS payment history for the period and match each deposit to its corresponding GL liability posting.
Confirm the liability account clears to zero after the deposit for the period.
Investigate and clear any variance before period close.
checklist.done: EFTPS deposits reconcile to GL postings with the liability account cleared for the period.

checklist.step: Track the cumulative deposit schedule to avoid a lookback-period reclassification
actions: Monitor the rolling 12-month lookback total withholding liability.
Recompute the deposit schedule threshold (the $50,000 look-back rule) at each quarter.
Notify Treasury Analyst immediately if the schedule must change mid-year.
checklist.done: the deposit schedule is recomputed each quarter and any required schedule change is communicated before the next deposit is due.

checklist.step: Escalate any missed or late deposit immediately
actions: Compute the IRC §6656 failure-to-deposit penalty exposure by days late and shortfall amount.
File the deposit as soon as possible and document the cause.
Consider a reasonable-cause penalty abatement request where warranted, prepared with Regulatory Counsel.
Report the miss to the Compliance Officer within one business day.
checklist.done: any missed deposit is remediated same-day, penalty exposure is computed, and the miss is reported within one business day.

checklist.step: Support payee withholding disputes with the computation record
actions: Retrieve the payment record showing the election/default applied and the computed rate for the disputed payment.
Determine whether the dispute is a corrected-election request (apply prospectively) or a claim of computational error (correct and reissue if verified).
Log the resolution and date.
checklist.done: every payee withholding dispute is resolved and logged with the applied correction, if any.

checklist.step: Reconcile the cycle's total withholding to the population extracted at intake
actions: Compare the count and dollar total of payments withheld against in the cycle to the original distribution extract.
Investigate any payment in the extract with no corresponding withholding computation.
Close out the reconciliation before the batch is archived.
checklist.done: every extracted payment has a corresponding withholding computation or a documented reason it was out of scope.

checklist.step: Retain the withholding computation and remittance evidence
actions: Save the withholding batch, manager approval, GL posting reference and EFTPS confirmation into the compliance evidence repository, indexed by cycle date.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the cycle's full withholding-to-remittance evidence chain is archived and retention-labeled.

checklist.step: Report the cycle's withholding and remittance status to Tax Director
actions: Summarize total withheld, total remitted, deposit timeliness and any open disputes/exceptions for the cycle.
Send the summary to Tax Director for sign-off.
File the signed summary with the cycle evidence.
checklist.done: a signed cycle summary of withholding and remittance status is filed with the cycle evidence.

testing.step: Build the population of withholding-eligible payments for the test period
actions: Extract every annuity, life cash-value and retirement distribution paid in the test period from the policy administration system.
Add the NRA and backup-withholding flags used at processing time.
Reconcile the extract total dollar amount to the GL disbursement account for the period.
testing.done: the population reconciles to GL disbursements and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the withholding computation batches
actions: Match each population payment to a withholding computation batch record on payment id.
List any payment with no matching computation as an automatic exception.
Confirm computed-withholding totals tie to the batches approved by Tax Manager.
testing.done: every population payment matches a computation batch or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of NRA and backup-withholding payments.
Take a random sample (seeded, reproducible) of 25 domestic payments from the remainder, minimum 40 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all NRA and backup-withholding payments.

testing.step: Re-perform the withholding rate computation for each sampled payment
actions: Independently look up the payee's election (W-4P/W-4R) or the applicable default, and the correct IRS Publication 15-T rate or treaty rate, without referencing the original computation.
Compute the expected withholding amount.
Compare to the amount actually applied and log any difference as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled payment has an independent re-performed computation compared to the applied amount.

testing.step: Verify treaty-rate claims on sampled NRA payments
actions: For each sampled NRA payment claiming a treaty rate, pull the Form W-8BEN on file.
Confirm it is signed, unexpired, and cites the correct treaty article for the payee's country.
Confirm the treaty rate applied matches the article.
Flag any expired or unsupported W-8BEN as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled treaty-rate claim is supported by a valid, unexpired W-8BEN citing the correct article.

testing.step: Trace each sampled remittance to its EFTPS deposit confirmation
actions: Pull the EFTPS confirmation number recorded against the sampled payment's batch.
Independently query EFTPS payment history to confirm the deposit was made, for the correct amount, before the deposit deadline.
Compute days-late, if any, and the resulting §6656 penalty exposure.
testing.done: every sampled remittance traces to a confirmed, timely EFTPS deposit, or a computed penalty exposure is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the deposit-schedule threshold for the test period
actions: Recompute the rolling 12-month lookback withholding total as of each sampled deposit date.
Confirm the semi-weekly/monthly schedule applied matches the recomputed threshold.
Flag any period where the wrong schedule was used.
testing.done: the deposit schedule applied in the sample matches the recomputed lookback threshold, or the mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Reconcile the GL withholding liability account to zero for each sampled period
actions: For each sampled period, pull the GL withholding payable sub-account activity.
Confirm the ending balance nets to zero after the EFTPS deposit.
Investigate any residual balance for a missed or partial deposit.
testing.done: the GL withholding liability account clears to zero for every sampled period or the residual is explained.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception (wrong rate, missing W-8BEN, late deposit, unreconciled liability).
Assign a root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and, for late-deposit breaches, open a penalty-abatement or self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into next cycle's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for late deposits and NRA misapplication.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled computations sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns timely, accurate issuance of policyholder tax forms; escalation to Tax Director

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IRC §6047/§6050Q/§6041/§3405 information-reporting requirements plus the current-year Form 1099-R/1099-INT/1099-LTC/1042-S instructions, re-read each filing season

In-scope processes.value: Year-end distribution extract → payee validation → form computation → furnish to payee → file with IRS, across all annuity, life, retirement and LTC payments including foreign payees

In-scope systems.value: Source of payment/payee data; forms are furnished electronically through the Customer Self-Service Portal where consented

Compliance procedure documented.value: Policyholder Tax Form Issuance Procedure — extraction, TIN matching, taxable amount/code computation, review, furnish, IRS filing, corrections

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Tax Director; reviewed annually against the current-year IRS form instructions and any distribution-code updates

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Furnish to payees by January 31 (March 15 for Form 1042-S); file with the IRS via FIRE/Form 1042 by March 31 (March 15 for 1042-S)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tax reporting calendar alerts at T-30/T-14/T-3 days ahead of the January 31 furnish deadline and the IRS filing deadlines

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Finalized form population, TIN Matching results, e-delivery consents and IRS transmission confirmations retained 7 years from the filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed furnish/file deadlines, TIN mismatches and consent gaps logged as exceptions with §6721/§6722 penalty exposure and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Tax Director signs off every late-issuance remediation and correction refiling

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All 1099-R, 1099-INT, 1099-LTC and 1042-S forms required for distributions, interest and LTC/accelerated benefit payments made in the tax year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a missed statutory furnish or file deadline, or an unactioned TIN mismatch; any fail escalates to Tax Director

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test runs once per filing season over the full year's population, with 100% coverage of Form 1042-S

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have generated or approved any sampled form

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policyholder-form test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed form set, FIRE/1042 transmission confirmations and TIN Matching results, presentable to an IRS examiner within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Tax Director owns the IRS information-return inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any penalty-abatement request

checklist.step: Extract the population of reportable payments for the tax year
actions: Run the year-end distributions report for all annuity, life surrender/withdrawal, retirement plan and LTC/accelerated death benefit payments made in the calendar year.
Include interest paid on delayed claims and death proceeds left on deposit.
Segment by required form type (1099-R, 1099-INT, 1099-LTC, 5498, 1042-S for foreign payees).
Export the segmented population to the tax reporting workpaper.
checklist.done: the full year's reportable-payment population is extracted and segmented by required form type.

checklist.step: Validate payee name, address and TIN against source records
actions: Match each payee record to the policy administration system's current name, address and TIN.
Run a TIN-match query through the IRS TIN Matching Program (e-Services) for every payee before form generation.
Flag mismatches for correction before forms are produced.
Where a TIN is missing, apply backup withholding per the withholding procedure and flag the record for a B-Notice.
checklist.done: every payee record passes TIN Matching or is flagged and corrected/backup-withheld before forms are generated.

checklist.step: Compute the taxable amount and distribution code for each 1099-R
actions: For each annuity/life/retirement distribution, compute the gross distribution and taxable amount per the investment-in-contract basis-recovery rules under §72.
Assign the correct IRS distribution code (e.g., 1 early, 2 exception, 4 death, 7 normal, G direct rollover, Q qualified Roth) per the payment's facts.
Record the code and taxable amount on the payee's form record.
checklist.done: every 1099-R payee record carries a correct taxable amount and IRS distribution code.

checklist.step: Compute LTC/accelerated death benefit reporting under §6050Q
actions: For accelerated death benefit and LTC payments, determine whether the per-diem or reimbursement basis applies.
Determine whether the payment is fully or partially excludable under §101(g)/§7702B.
Populate the Form 1099-LTC boxes for gross benefits paid and the per-diem/reimbursement indicator.
checklist.done: every LTC/accelerated benefit payment has a correctly populated 1099-LTC record.

checklist.step: Generate the draft form set and route for manager review
actions: Generate the draft 1099-R, 1099-INT, 1099-LTC and 1042-S forms from the validated payee records.
Sample-check 15 forms across form types for correct box population against source payment records.
Approve the draft set for finalization or return exceptions to Tax Analyst.
checklist.done: the draft form set is reviewed and approved, or exceptions are returned and corrected.

checklist.step: Finalize and prepare forms for delivery
actions: Lock the approved form set from further edits.
Generate paper copies for payees without an e-delivery consent on file, and electronic files for those who consented.
Confirm the finalized set count matches the approved draft count.
checklist.done: the finalized form set matches the approved draft count and is split correctly between paper and electronic delivery.

checklist.step: Confirm e-delivery consent before electronic issuance
actions: In the Customer Self-Service Portal, pull the list of policyholders who affirmatively consented to electronic tax-form delivery per the IRS e-delivery consent rules.
Confirm the consent record includes the required disclosures (hardware/software needed, right to request paper, withdrawal method) and predates this filing.
Exclude anyone without valid consent from electronic delivery and route them to paper.
checklist.done: every electronically delivered form has a valid, dated e-delivery consent on file; all others are routed to paper.

checklist.step: Furnish forms to payees by the statutory deadline
actions: Mail paper forms and post electronic forms to the Customer Self-Service Portal no later than January 31 following the tax year.
Furnish Form 1042-S by March 15.
Log the furnish date for each delivery batch.
checklist.done: every payee form is furnished (mailed or posted) by its statutory deadline, with the furnish date logged.

checklist.step: File the forms with the IRS via the required system
actions: Transmit Form 1099-R, 1099-INT and 1099-LTC to the IRS through the IRS FIRE (Filing Information Returns Electronically) system before the e-file deadline of March 31.
Transmit Form 1042-S and the transmittal Form 1042 by March 15.
Retain the FIRE transmission confirmation and the Form 1042 e-file acceptance acknowledgment.
checklist.done: all forms are filed with the IRS through the required system before their deadline, with a transmission confirmation retained.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed totals to the general ledger and the extracted population
actions: Sum the gross distribution and withholding amounts across all filed forms by type.
Agree the totals to the GL distribution and withholding payable accounts for the year.
Agree the form count to the original population extract.
Resolve any variance before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: filed form totals reconcile to both the GL and the original population extract.

checklist.step: Handle undeliverable and corrected forms
actions: Process returned/undeliverable mail by researching the current address in the policy administration system and re-mailing.
For any error discovered after issuance, prepare a corrected form (with the 'CORRECTED' box checked, or an amended 1042-S) and refile with the IRS through FIRE.
Log every correction with the original and corrected values.
checklist.done: every undeliverable form is re-mailed and every post-issuance error is corrected and refiled, both logged.

checklist.step: Respond to payee inquiries and duplicate-form requests
actions: Log each payee inquiry disputing a reported amount or requesting a duplicate form.
Verify the reported figures against the source payment record before responding.
Issue a duplicate form through the Customer Self-Service Portal or by mail within 5 business days of a verified request.
checklist.done: every payee inquiry is verified against source records and resolved or a duplicate issued within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Escalate deadline risk before the furnish/file dates
actions: Monitor the count of forms not yet finalized against the days remaining to the January 31 furnish deadline and the March 31/March 15 file deadlines.
Where the count at T-5 business days shows risk of missing the deadline, escalate for additional resourcing.
Document the escalation and its resolution.
checklist.done: any deadline-risk condition is escalated and resolved before the statutory deadline, with the escalation documented.

checklist.step: Retain the year's form population, filing confirmations and correction log
actions: Archive the finalized form population, IRS FIRE/1042 transmission confirmations, e-delivery consent records and the correction log into the compliance evidence repository, indexed by tax year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the full year's form-issuance evidence chain is archived and retention-labeled.

checklist.step: Report the year's issuance and filing status to Tax Director
actions: Summarize forms furnished on time, filed on time, corrections issued and any unresolved undeliverable forms.
Send the summary to Tax Director for sign-off.
File the signed summary with the year's evidence.
checklist.done: a signed year-end summary of form issuance and filing status is filed with the year's evidence.

testing.step: Build the population of forms required to be issued for the tax year
actions: Independently extract every reportable distribution/interest/LTC payment from the policy administration system for the tax year.
Reconcile the count and dollar total to the GL distribution accounts for the year.
Add any payment the Tax team's population may have missed based on payment-type codes.
testing.done: the population reconciles to GL and is signed as complete, including any items the original extract missed.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the filed form set
actions: Match each population payment to a filed 1099-R/1099-INT/1099-LTC/1042-S record on payee id and payment date.
List any payment with no matching filed form as an automatic exception.
Confirm form-type assignment (e.g., LTC vs 1099-R) is correct for each match.
testing.done: every population payment matches a filed form of the correct type, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of Form 1042-S (foreign payee) forms.
Take a random sample (seeded, reproducible) of 25 domestic forms across 1099-R/1099-INT/1099-LTC, minimum 40 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and includes every 1042-S form.

testing.step: Re-perform the taxable amount and distribution code computation for sampled 1099-R forms
actions: Independently compute the taxable amount under the §72 basis-recovery rules and the expected distribution code from the underlying payment facts, without referencing the issued form.
Compare to the code and amount on the issued form.
Log any difference as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled 1099-R has an independent re-performed computation compared to the issued form.

testing.step: Verify TIN Matching was performed before issuance for the sample
actions: Pull the IRS TIN Matching Program result for each sampled payee and confirm it was run before the form's generation date.
Confirm any mismatch was flagged and either corrected or backup-withheld.
Treat an unmatched TIN with no backup withholding applied as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled payee shows a pre-issuance TIN Match result, correctly actioned.

testing.step: Trace furnish and file dates against the statutory deadlines
actions: For each sampled form, pull the furnish date (mail log or Customer Self-Service Portal post date) and the IRS FIRE/1042 transmission date.
Compare both to the statutory deadlines (January 31 furnish, March 31/March 15 file).
Flag any form furnished or filed late.
testing.done: every sampled form's furnish and file dates are checked against the statutory deadline, with any late form flagged.

testing.step: Verify e-delivery consent for electronically issued sampled forms
actions: For each sampled form delivered electronically, pull the consent record from the Customer Self-Service Portal.
Confirm the consent predates the form and includes the required IRS disclosures.
Treat a missing or post-dated consent as a fail requiring the form to have been mailed instead.
testing.done: every sampled electronic form has a valid, pre-dated e-delivery consent, or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Recompute the reconciliation between filed totals, GL and the population extract
actions: For the sampled form types, recompute the aggregate gross distribution and withholding totals.
Compare to the GL and the original population extract.
Investigate any variance beyond a de minimis rounding threshold.
testing.done: recomputed totals reconcile to GL and the population extract, or the variance is explained.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception (missing form, wrong code/amount, late furnish/file, unmatched TIN, invalid consent).
Assign a root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and, for missed statutory deadlines, assess §6721/§6722 penalty exposure with Tax Director.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed statutory deadlines.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled issuance sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns scoping and timely filing of all information returns including FATCA/CRS; escalation to Tax Director

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IRC §6041/§6041A (1099 information returns) and Chapter 4 §§1471-1474 (FATCA) plus the applicable IGA and Common Reporting Standard rules, re-read each filing season for threshold and schema updates

In-scope processes.value: Year-end AP commission/vendor extract and foreign-account identification → self-certification validation → form/report preparation → IRS/IDES/CRS-portal transmission, covering all domestic payees and foreign-owned accounts

In-scope systems.value: Source of commission/vendor AP payments; FATCA/CRS filing status is tracked in the Internal Regulatory System filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Information Return Filing Procedure (1099/FATCA/CRS) — scoping, extraction, TIN/self-certification validation, preparation, transmission, reconciliation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Tax Director; reviewed annually against updated IRS thresholds, the IDES schema and each CRS jurisdiction's reporting rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: 1099-NEC due January 31; Form 8966 (FATCA) due March 31 via IDES; CRS filings due per each participating jurisdiction's deadline, commonly May 31

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts at T-45/T-15 days ahead of the January 31, March 31 and jurisdiction-specific CRS deadlines

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed 1099s, Form 8966, CRS submissions, transmission confirmations and self-certifications retained 7 years from the filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed filings, invalid self-certifications and late transmissions logged as exceptions with penalty exposure and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Tax Director signs off every late-filing remediation and recalcitrant-account determination

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All 1099-NEC/MISC reportable commission and vendor payments, plus every FATCA-reportable and CRS-reportable policy account, for the tax year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a missed FATCA/CRS deadline or an unremediated recalcitrant account; ≤2% exception rate tolerated on domestic 1099s before escalation

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test runs once per filing season over the full population, with 100% coverage of FATCA/CRS accounts

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or transmitted any sampled filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual information-return test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed 1099/8966/CRS set with IDES/portal confirmations, presentable to an IRS or foreign tax authority examiner within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Tax Director owns the IRS/FATCA/CRS inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any cross-border information exchange dispute

checklist.step: Identify all information-return obligations in scope for the year
actions: Review the prior year's filing checklist against this year's business activity (producer commission payments, foreign-owned policy accounts, non-US branch operations).

Confirm which forms apply: 1099-MISC/NEC for commissions/vendor payments at or above $600, Form 8966 for FATCA-reportable accounts, and CRS reporting for any jurisdiction where the company operates as a Reporting Financial Institution.
Document the scope decision and its basis.
checklist.done: a documented scope decision names every information-return type required for the year and its basis.

checklist.step: Extract the population of reportable commission and vendor payments
actions: Run the accounts-payable report for all producer/agent commission and non-employee vendor payments in the calendar year.
Filter to payees with cumulative payments at or above the $600 reporting threshold.
Exclude corporations unless the payment is for legal services (which remain reportable) or medical/health payments.
Export the payee list with TINs.
checklist.done: the commission/vendor payment population is extracted, thresholded and exported with payee TINs.

checklist.step: Identify FATCA-reportable financial accounts
actions: Query the policy administration system for cash-value life and annuity contracts owned by foreign persons or foreign entities meeting the FATCA 'financial account' and threshold tests under the applicable Model 1/Model 2 IGA or Chapter 4 regulations.
Confirm each account has a valid Form W-8BEN-E/self-certification supporting its FATCA classification.
Flag any account with a missing or stale self-certification.
checklist.done: the FATCA-reportable account population is identified with self-certification status flagged for each.

checklist.step: Identify CRS-reportable accounts for applicable foreign jurisdictions
actions: For each non-US branch/subsidiary operating as a Reporting Financial Institution under a CRS-participating jurisdiction, query that entity's policy records for reportable accounts held by tax residents of CRS partner jurisdictions.
Confirm self-certifications of tax residency are on file.
Flag accounts with missing self-certifications for remediation before the filing deadline.
checklist.done: the CRS-reportable account population per jurisdiction is identified with self-certification status flagged.

checklist.step: Validate TINs on the 1099 population via TIN Matching
actions: Submit the commission/vendor payee list to the IRS TIN Matching Program via e-Services before form generation.
Flag any non-match for a B-Notice and apply backup withholding on future payments until resolved.
Log match results against each payee.
checklist.done: every 1099 payee has a logged TIN Matching result, with non-matches actioned.

checklist.step: Prepare and review the 1099-MISC/NEC form set
actions: Generate draft 1099-NEC (nonemployee compensation, box 1) and 1099-MISC (other reportable payments) forms from the validated payee population.
Sample 10 forms against the underlying AP payment detail.
Approve the set for finalization or return exceptions.
checklist.done: the 1099-MISC/NEC draft set is reviewed and approved, or exceptions are returned and corrected.

checklist.step: Furnish 1099-MISC/NEC forms to payees and file with the IRS
actions: Mail or electronically deliver 1099-NEC/1099-MISC to payees by January 31.
Transmit the forms to the IRS through the FIRE system by January 31 for 1099-NEC (no automatic extension) and by March 31 for 1099-MISC if e-filed.
Retain the FIRE transmission confirmation.
checklist.done: 1099-NEC/MISC forms are furnished and filed by their respective statutory deadlines with a transmission confirmation retained.

checklist.step: Prepare the FATCA Form 8966 report
actions: Populate Form 8966 for each FATCA-reportable account with the account balance, income paid, and account holder identifying information per the applicable IGA reporting requirements.
Route the draft to Tax Manager for review against the flagged account population.
checklist.done: a draft Form 8966 exists for every flagged FATCA-reportable account, reconciled to the population.

checklist.step: Transmit the FATCA report through the IRS FATCA IDES portal
actions: Log in to the IRS FATCA International Data Exchange Service (IDES) using the company's Global Intermediary Identification Number (GIIN).
Package and encrypt the Form 8966 XML file per IDES specifications.
Submit before the FATCA filing deadline (March 31 following the reporting year, or the applicable IGA deadline).
Retain the IDES transmission receipt and status.
checklist.done: the FATCA XML file is submitted through IDES before the deadline with a retained transmission receipt showing accepted status.

checklist.step: Transmit CRS reports through each applicable jurisdiction's portal
actions: For each CRS-reporting jurisdiction, format the account data per that jurisdiction's CRS XML schema.
Log in to the local tax authority's CRS filing portal and submit before that jurisdiction's deadline (commonly May 31 following the calendar year, confirmed per jurisdiction).
Retain the portal's submission confirmation.
checklist.done: every applicable jurisdiction's CRS report is submitted before its deadline with a retained confirmation.

checklist.step: Reconcile all filed information returns to the source population
actions: Sum the payment/account totals across all filed 1099, 8966 and CRS reports.
Agree the totals to the ERP accounts-payable ledger and the policy administration account extracts used to build the population.
Resolve variances before closing the filing cycle.
checklist.done: filed return totals reconcile to both the ERP ledger and the policy administration extracts.

checklist.step: Remediate missing self-certifications before the next filing cycle
actions: Send a remediation request to the account holder or servicing team for accounts flagged with missing/stale FATCA or CRS self-certifications.
Escalate uncured accounts past 90 days to Tax Director for a recalcitrant-account determination and possible 30% FATCA withholding on US-source payments.
checklist.done: every flagged self-certification is remediated or, if uncured past 90 days, escalated with a recalcitrant determination.

checklist.step: Escalate any missed filing deadline immediately
actions: File as soon as possible and document the cause where a 1099, 8966 or CRS deadline is missed.
Compute the IRC §6721/§6722 penalty exposure for late/incorrect information returns, or the applicable IGA penalty for late FATCA/CRS filing.
Report the miss to the Compliance Officer within one business day.
checklist.done: any missed filing is remediated promptly with penalty exposure computed and reported within one business day.

checklist.step: Retain the year's filed returns, transmission confirmations and self-certifications
actions: Archive the filed 1099 set, Form 8966, CRS submissions, IDES/portal confirmations and account self-certifications into the compliance evidence repository, indexed by tax year and jurisdiction.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the full year's information-return evidence chain is archived and retention-labeled.

checklist.step: Report the year's filing status to the Compliance Committee
actions: Summarize forms/reports filed on time, any missed deadlines, recalcitrant-account determinations and open remediation.
Present the summary at the next Compliance Committee sitting.
Record the committee's disposition.
checklist.done: the year's information-return filing status is reported to the Compliance Committee with a recorded disposition.

testing.step: Build the population of information returns required for the year
actions: Independently extract the commission/vendor AP payments at or above the $600 threshold from the ERP ledger.
Independently query the policy administration system for foreign-owned accounts meeting FATCA/CRS thresholds.
Reconcile both extracts to the Tax team's documented scope decision.
testing.done: the population is independently rebuilt and reconciles to the documented scope decision.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the filed return set
actions: Match each population item (payee or account) to a filed 1099, Form 8966 record or CRS submission line.
List any unmatched item as an automatic exception.
Confirm form-type assignment is correct.
testing.done: every population item matches a filed return of the correct type, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of FATCA-reportable and CRS-reportable accounts.
Take a random sample (seeded, reproducible) of 25 domestic 1099 payees, minimum 40 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of FATCA/CRS accounts.

testing.step: Re-perform TIN Matching verification for sampled 1099 payees
actions: Independently query the IRS TIN Matching Program result for each sampled payee.
Confirm the result was obtained before form generation and any non-match was actioned with a B-Notice and backup withholding.
Log any unactioned non-match as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled payee's TIN Match status is independently verified and correctly actioned.

testing.step: Verify FATCA/CRS self-certifications for sampled accounts
actions: Pull the self-certification (W-8BEN-E or CRS self-certification form) on file for each sampled account.
Confirm it is signed, unexpired, and supports the FATCA/CRS classification and reported account holder details used in the filing.
Flag any missing or stale certification as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled account's self-certification is valid and supports the filed classification, or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Trace filing transmissions to IDES/CRS portal confirmations
actions: For sampled FATCA accounts, confirm the account appears in the transmitted Form 8966 XML and the IDES receipt shows accepted status.
For sampled CRS accounts, confirm inclusion in the jurisdiction's submitted file and a retained portal confirmation.
Flag any account present in the population but absent from the transmission.
testing.done: every sampled FATCA/CRS account traces to an accepted transmission, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute deadline compliance for each filing type
actions: Compare the recorded transmission date for 1099s, Form 8966 and each CRS jurisdiction's submission to its statutory deadline (January 31 for 1099-NEC, March 31 for FATCA, jurisdiction-specific for CRS).
Flag any late transmission and compute the applicable penalty exposure.
testing.done: every filing type's transmission date is checked against its deadline, with any late filing flagged and penalty exposure computed.

testing.step: Reconcile filed totals to the ERP ledger and account extracts
actions: Recompute the aggregate payment/account totals across the sampled filings.
Compare to the ERP AP ledger and policy administration extracts.
Investigate any variance beyond a de minimis rounding threshold.
testing.done: recomputed totals reconcile to the ERP ledger and account extracts, or the variance is explained.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception (missing filing, wrong form type, invalid self-certification, late transmission).
Assign a root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and, for late FATCA/CRS filings, assess penalty exposure with Regulatory Counsel and Tax Director.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed FATCA/CRS deadlines.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled filings sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.
